biography: Renger van der Zande, a native of the Netherlands, didn't come from a racing dynasty. His father ran a small bicycle repair shop, a world away from the roar of engines. However, a chance visit to the Zandvoort circuit at age 10 ignited an unquenchable passion. He badgered his parents until they relented, starting him in karting. Progress was steady, if unspectacular, until a breakthrough victory in a national karting championship caught the eye of a local motorsport patron. This led to a gradual climb through the formula ranks, culminating in a transition to sports car racing. His aggressive style initially caused collisions and damaged equipment, but he refined his approach over time. Now, as a seasoned driver for Cadillac, he aims to leave a mark on endurance racing, seeking overall wins at Daytona and Le Mans.
drivingStyle: Van der Zande's driving style is a blend of controlled aggression and calculated risk. He's known for his late-braking maneuvers and willingness to push the car to its absolute limit, often teetering on the edge of control. While he has matured over the years, the instinct to attack is always present. Tire management has been an area of focus, as his early career was plagued by excessive wear due to his hard-charging approach. He thrives under pressure, often delivering his best performances when the stakes are highest.

rivalries.reason: A bitter rivalry stemming from a controversial last-lap incident at the 24 Hours of Daytona, where Rossi's aggressive move forced van der Zande off the track, costing him the victory.
A technical rivalry. Tanaka consistently outpaces van der Zande in wet conditions, leading to a constant battle to understand and improve wet-weather performance relative to each other.

famousQuote: Sometimes, you have to risk it for the biscuit. Second place is just the first loser.
careerHighlight: Winning the 24 Hours of Spa in 2016, overcoming mechanical issues and intense pressure to secure a dominant victory for his team.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead in the final hour of the 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2018, a mistake that cost his team a likely victory and left him deeply disappointed.
